﻿Isl202 assignment 1
Spring 2022
Our lives are a continuous succession of God’s gifts. Allah has made it clear that we will never be able to count all of His blessings upon us, since they are innumerable.
ALLAH Almighty says: “And if you were to count Allah’s favors, you would not be able to number them; most surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
But here we’re going to discuss any four of them.
Milk:
We give you to drink of that which is in their (cattle’s) bellies, between the dung and the blood: pure milk, a pleasant beverage for those who drink it.(16:66)
Milk is great blessing from Allah for all of us. It is a pure liquid which is very nutritious and beneficial for our health. It gives us good bone health, strong immune system etc. According to Holy Prophet (SAW) Milk of cow can treat any type of pain and ache.
Parents:
 And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, “My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up (when I was) small.
Parents are the most precious blessing of Allah. They are the luckiest people in this world who have their parents alive. Parents are like a pillar, a shade, the biggest support of our lives.  Our parents are like a shield which protects you not just in this world but also hereafter by the grace and will of Allah.
Waking up today and being alive:
And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day and your seeking of His bounty, verily in that are signs for those who hearken”
Today is a blessing that allows us to live in the present while enabling us to review our past and plan for a better tomorrow. Waking up to see another day is a blessing. Don’t take it for granted. Make it count and be happy that you are alive.
Water:
“And We have sent down blessed rain from the sky and made grow thereby gardens and grain from the harvest
In the Qur’an, Allah uses the analogy of life and death for Muslims to recognize the value of water. We have taps that fill our basins with gold, but we cannot afford overflows while people wait for the rains. Third-world countries in desert climates are counting on us to give the cost of our water to them.  rain is a blessing. We need it to fill lakes and streams, which provide sources of drinking water and crop irrigation
Weather patterns:
It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds and spread them in the sky however He wills, and He makes them fragments so you see the rain emerge from within them. And when He causes it to fall upon whom He wills of His servants, immediately they rejoice.
Weather affects us in a huge number of ways. Climate influences the growth of crops, thus affecting the availability and kind of food we eat. Fluctuations in weather (e.g. dry spells, wet spells) also affect crops. Weather affects what clothes we wear, and soon.

Juma:
O you who believe (Muslims)! When the call is proclaimed for the Salat (prayer) on Friday (Jumu’ah prayer), come to the remembrance of Allah [Jumu’ah religious talk (Khutbah) and Salat (prayer)] and leave off business (and every other thing). That is better for you if you did but know!

1
ترجمہ: درحقیقت اللہ کے رسول (صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم) میں تمہارے لیے ہر اس شخص کے لیے بہترین اور خوبصورت نمونہ (زندگی کا) موجود ہے جو اللہ سے ملاقات کی امید رکھتا ہے اور اس کی تمنا رکھتا ہے۔ آخرت کے دن اور اللہ کو کثرت سے یاد کرتے ہیں۔

10)

11-

ترجمہ: بے شک اللہ اور (سب) اس کے فرشتے حضور (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) پر درود و سلام بھیجتے ہیں۔ اے ایمان والو! اس پر درود بھیجا کرو اور اس پر کثرت سے (اور جوش سے) سلام کرو۔

12-
ترجمہ: بے شک جو لوگ اللہ اور اس کے رسول کو اذیت دیتے ہیں اللہ ان پر دنیا اور آخرت میں لعنت کرتا ہے اور اس نے ان کے لیے رسوا کن عذاب تیار کر رکھا ہے۔
13-

ترجمہ: اور جو لوگ مومن مردوں اور مومن عورتوں کو بغیر کسی غلط کام کے ایذا دیتے ہیں، وہ یقیناً جھوٹے الزام اور کھلے گناہ کا بوجھ اٹھاتے ہیں۔

14-
ترجمہ: اور رحمٰن (رب) کے (پسندیدہ) بندے وہ ہیں جو زمین پر نرمی سے چلتے ہیں، اور جب جاہل (یعنی بے حیائی) لوگ ان سے کوئی بات (ناپسند) کہتے ہیں تو وہ (ایک طرف ہو جاتے ہیں) کہتے ہیں: "امن"۔
15-

ترجمہ: اور (یہ) وہ لوگ ہیں جو خرچ کرتے وقت نہ اسراف کرتے ہیں اور نہ بخل کرتے ہیں۔ اور ان کا خرچ (اس کی بنیاد پر) دو انتہاؤں (اسراف اور کنجوسی) کے درمیان توازن ہے۔

acknowledge that for our guidance God had vouchsafed to them knowledge that was beyond the range of

                      1. Allah exists and nobody created Him.

                         the universe according to His will.
                      4. He alone is to be exclusively worshipped and He has no associates.
  The existence of Allah
          The Qur’an has clearly told us that the proof of the existence of Allah lies within ourselves. How
          can we, then deny something which is writ large on our very foreheads as the proof of its veracity
          Allah says.

          misfortune, we seek his shelter because of our faithful nature and religious instinct. There are,
          within us and all around us numerous proofs of His existence. Our sub conscious that is our
          heart, unconsciously in Him, but our conscious self, that is our reason, accepts His existence.

ISL202
                                    Glossary

 A.H
means After Hijrah. It is the reference used in the Islamic calendar, instead of A.D. which is used
in the Christian calendar
 Abu dawud
Abu sulayman ibn al-ash'ath ibn ishaq al-azdi as-sijistani, the author of the sunan and one of the
greatest of the scholars of hadith. he was born in 203/817 and died on a friday in the middle of
shawwal, 275/888 in basra. he was so accomplished in the science of hadith that it was said that
hadiths were made pliable for abu dawud in the same way that iron was made pliable for the
prophet da'ud. he said, "i wrote down 500,000 hadiths of the prophet and selected from them those
which are in the sunan." he was a pupil of ibn hanbal.
 Abu hanifa
Abu hanifa an-nu`man ibn thabit, founder of the hanafi school in baghdad. he is one of the four
imams and is known for developing ra'y (judicial opinion). he shunned sleep and was called the
"peg" because he used to stand for long periods in night prayers. he only slept between zuhr and
asr. he grew up in kufa and the khalif al-mansur asked him to accept the post of qadi. he refused
and al-mansur imprisoned him and beat him until he died. he would never sit in the shade of
someone to whom he had loaned money, saying, "every loan that brings benefit is usury." he died
in 150/767.(
 Abu yusuf
Ya`qub ibn ibrahim ibn habib al-ansari al-baghdadi, born in kufa in 113/731. he was the student
of abu hanifa and the first to propagate his school, a hadith master and brilliant jurist who had an
extensive knowledge of tafsir. he acted as qadi in baghdad for al-mahdi, al-hadi and harun ar-
rashid, who made the hanafi school the official state code for the 'abbasids. he was also the first to
write on the principles (usul) of hanafi fiqh, and was a mujtahid. he died in baghdad in 182/798.
he wrote kitab al-kharaj on taxation and constitutional questions.
 Adam (aa-dum)
The first human being, created by God as His vicegerent (responsible deputy) on Earth. Muslims
believe Adam was the first prophet of God as well, establishing monotheism as the original

Maha Malik’s Compilation

spiritual system of humankind. Islam does not share with Christianity the doctrine of "Original
Sin," instead maintaining that each individual person is born sinless and is responsible for his or
her own spiritual state, independent of the actions of other persons, past or present.
 Adhan ‫اذان‬
The Muslim call to worship. The adhan consists of specific phrases, recited aloud in Arabic prior
to each of the five daily worship times. Upon hearing the adhan, Muslims discontinue all activity
and assemble at a local masjid for formal communal worship.
 Badr
The first full military confrontation between the Muslims and the enemies of Allah. The battle
took place between the Muslims and the Quraish of Mecca in the second year of Hijrah (624 C.E.).
Eventhough the Muslims were outnumbered, the final result was to their favor
 Bai'
Literally means sale. Commonly used as a prefix in referring to different types of sales: Muajjal,
Murabahah, Tawliyah and Wadi'ah.
 Baligh
One who is has reached the age of maturity
 Banni isra'il
The tribe of israel, the children or descendants of israel or ya`qub.
 Baqi
The cemetery where a good many of the Sahabah are buried. It is in the south-east side of Madinah.
 C.E.
stands for Christian Era. It is used instead of A.D. in Islamic text referring to the dates before the
Hijrah.
 Calendar, muslim
A lunar calendar whose months are: muharram, safar, rabi' al-awwal, rabi' ath-thani, jumada al-
ula, jumada alakhira, rajah, sha`ban, ramadan, shawwal, dhu'l-qa`da, dhu'lhijja. the lunar year is
approximately eleven days shorter than the solar year.

Adhan

Inviting or calling people to worship Allah by following the messenger of Allah.

himself, his Father, and the Holy Spirit. Sent to Earth to atone for the sins of mankind, Jesus was
born in the town of Bethlehem, around 5 BCE, to mortal parents by virginal birth. His mother on
Earth was Mary, his father Joseph. In Catholic doctrine, Mary -- whose own conception is referred
to as the Imaculate Conception; being born without any stain of 'original sin' -- was elevated to the

three years on the Earth, explaining to the large and ever-expanding following he attracted the
mysteries of his kingdom, the Kingdom of Heaven, and how people could attain that wonderful
place. He gathered to him twelve acolytes, or Apostles, whom he later sent out into the world on
their own, to cast out demons and bring the true word of God to the masses.

Definition of faith
Belief in the special terminology of Islam, means to believe in the Prophets of God as such, that is to
acknowledge that for our guidance God had vouchsafed to them knowledge that was beyond the range of
our intelligence and understanding, and, on the basis of it, to affirm what was communicated to us by them
as from God, and to accept religion brought by them as Divine religion.

Lecture# 16:                              Forgiveness
Definition of Forgiveness
      To free or pardon (someone) from penalty
      To free from the obligation of (a debt, payment, etc.).
Pardon and Forgiveness
        Once at the time of Asr (Middle prayer) in a speech to the people the Messenger of Allah said:
"Adam's sons have been created of different types. There are some who get angry late and very soon
return to normal. Some people become wrathful soon and soon they return to normal, and some people
become angry late and are also late in returning to normal that is the return to normalcy is according to the
speed of getting angry.
        Be careful. Some people get angry soon and they return to normal late. Listen, the best people
among these are those who get angry late and immediately repent, and the worst among these are those
who get angry soon, but are very late in coming to normal.
        Listen, among these there are some who repay the loan in a better way, and also demand in a good
way. Some people are lazy in repaying, but good in demanding. Some demand in a bad way and repay in a
good way, i.e. they have one good quality and one bad quality. Some people prove to be bad in demanding
and in repaying too.
         Listen carefully, the best among these are those who are good in demanding and also good in

What is the definition of faith in the Islamic context?
A) Belief in divine terminology
B) Acknowledgment of historical events
C) Recognition of cultural practices
D) Understanding of societal norms

According to the passage, what constitutes the basic principles of faith in Islam?
A) Respect for cultural diversity
B) Belief in scientific advancements
C) Faith in Allah, prophets, and the Hereafter
D) Adherence to political ideologies

What is the primary premise of faith in Allah as described in the text?
A) Belief in multiple creators
B) Denial of a divine entity
C) Recognition of Allah's sole existence and creation
D) Worship of nature's elements

According to the Qur'an, where does the proof of Allah's existence lie?
A) Within our conscience
B) In external written scriptures
C) Among scientific discoveries
D) Through social interactions

What does it mean to believe that Allah is the Sustainer of the whole Universe?
A) He solely creates living organisms
B) He collaborates with other deities
C) He intervenes only in visible worlds
D) He has no knowledge of scientific principles

What does the passage suggest about acknowledging Allah as the Master of the
universe?
A) He doesn't interfere with His creation
B) He has limited knowledge of His creations
C) He continuously alters and oversees His creation
D) He delegates control to other entities

What is highlighted as a crucial aspect of being a believer in Allah?
A) Mere declaration of faith

B) Association with ancient nations
C) Following cultural traditions
D) Engaging in rituals

What distinguishes a believer from those who merely declare Allah's existence?
A) Engagement in philosophical debates
B) Adherence to societal norms
C) Acceptance of Allah as the sole deity to worship
D) Engaging in scientific discoveries

What follows logically when one acknowledges Allah's existence and role as the
Sustainer of the worlds?
A) Acknowledgment of multiple deities
B) Embrace of atheistic beliefs
C) Rejection of religious practices
D) Exclusivity in worshipping Allah

What is the primary emphasis concerning the worship of Allah?
A) Exclusivity and denial of other deities
B) Inclusion of cultural deities
C) Worship through multiple forms
D) Recognition of diverse religious beliefs

How many premises form the basis of faith in Allah as outlined in the text?
A) Two premises
B) Three premises
C) Four premises
D) Five premises

What is the primary reason given in the text for seeking Allah's shelter during
hardships?
A) Cultural conditioning
B) Instinctual faith and religious nature
C) Social pressures
D) Historical beliefs

What is the core message of Surah An-Nas (114)?
A. Exalting the prophets' divinity
B. Emphasizing the unity of Allah
C. Discussing the life after death
D. Explaining the miracles of prophets

What distinct characteristic do the Prophets possess according to the text?

A. Eternal life
B. Divinity
C. Receiving revelations
D. Exceptional physical strength

Which premise is NOT part of faith in the Prophets?
A. Islam's unbiased view of Prophets
B. Divinity of all Prophets
C. Acceptance of Prophets as human
D. Belief in the miracles of Prophets

How does Islam view disrespect toward any Prophet?
A. It's tolerated if justified
B. It's considered permissible
C. It's condemned and against Islamic principles
D. It's seen as a sign of independence

What distinguishes Prophets from others?
A. Physical appearance
B. Immortality
C. Divine powers
D. Revelation from Allah

Which type of "impossible" occurrence is exemplified by the Ascension?
A. Common impossible
B. Rationally impossible
C. Unbelievable impossible
D. Physically impossible

What analogy does the Prophet use to explain resurrection?
A. A barren land turning green
B. Sunrise after a dark night
C. Changing seasons
D. A seed growing into a tree

According to the text, what is a significant fruit of faith?
A. Atonement for sins
B. Consistent remembrance of Allah
C. Material wealth
D. Superior physical health
Answer: B. Consistent remembrance of Allah

What is the Surah that emphasizes the unity of Allah?
A. Surah Al-Fatiha

B. Surah Al-Ikhlas
C. Surah Al-Baqarah
D. Surah An-Nas

What do all Prophets have in common regarding their nature?
A. They are eternal beings
B. They are completely divine
C. They possess the ability to perform miracles
D. They are human beings

What reaction did people have to the Prophet's Ascension during his time?
A. Complete disbelief
B. Acceptance without question
C. Amazement but belief
D. It wasn't recorded

According to Islamic belief, what is the Hereafter considered to be?
A. An extension of this life
B. The end of existence
C. A temporary halt between worlds
D. An illusionary concept

Which characteristic defines the attitude epitomized by the Prophet regarding
worship?
A. Perfectionism
B. Compassion
C. Utmost sincerity
D. Recognition of divinity

What type of occurrence becomes possible through scientific progress, as
mentioned in the text?
A. Rationally impossible
B. Miraculous occurrences
C. Commonplace impossible
D. Unbelievably impossible

Which Surah emphasizes the belief in the unity of Allah?
A. Surah Al-Fatiha
B. Surah Al-Ikhlas
C. Surah Al-Baqarah
D. Surah An-Nas

                           LECTURE # 02
What is the meaning of Taqwa according to the Messenger of Allah?

A) Fear of the unknown
B) Awareness and consciousness of Allah
C) Following the path of light
D) Obeying the societal norms

What does the Quran emphasize as a result of having Taqwa?
A) Forgiveness and guidance
B) Wealth and prosperity
C) Power and authority
D) Fame and recognition

According to various scholars, what does "Furqaan" mean in the context of
Taqwa?
A) Enlightenment only in this world
B) A way out from difficulty
C) Guidance for the Hereafter
D) Salvation from all hardships

What does Taqwa primarily aim to do to the heart and soul?
A) Enrich them with worldly pleasures
